scenarios.name: Discover current-user IPv4 and IPv6 listeners without port allowlists
scenarios.setup: Two dev servers owned by current user: HTTP on 127.0.0.1:41937 (uncommon high port) and Vite-style dev server on [::1]:5173, plus a wildcard server on 0.0.0.0:8088.

scenarios.name: Separate openable HTML Web UIs from Swagger/OpenAPI, Chrome DevTools, JSON APIs, and raw TCP
scenarios.setup: Five local listeners: (a) attributed HTML Web UI in a Git repo, (b) /docs Swagger HTML stub, (c) Chromium /json/version endpoint, (d) unattributed JSON API, (e) raw TCP echo socket.

scenarios.name: Attribute owning project cleanly and strip Git remote credentials
scenarios.setup: Node/Python app started from repo subdir with embedded credential remote URL https://user:secret-token@github.com/acme/demo-app.git and runtime files under node_modules / .venv/site-packages.

scenarios.name: Keep distinct Git worktrees separated
scenarios.setup: Main checkout on branch main running app A on port 3101; linked git worktree on feat/proxy running app A copy on port 3102.

scenarios.name: Attribute host-published Docker listener to container metadata and refuse daemon kill
scenarios.setup: Host port 54321 published by container runtime (com.docker.backend / dockerd / docker-proxy) backed by postgres:16 container.

scenarios.name: Reverse proxy HTTP, WebSocket upgrade, SSE streaming, and IPv6-only upstreams over *.localhost
scenarios.setup: Aliased web-ipv6.localhost -> [::1]:{p1} (HTML + SSE) and web-ws.localhost -> 127.0.0.1:{p2} (WebSocket echo), reached via loopback proxy Host header (case-insensitive with :port suffix).

scenarios.name: Rebind alias across port/PID restart and reject alias collisions
scenarios.setup: Assign alias 'web' to app A on port 4001. Restart app A on new PID and port 4002 under same project/worktree identity. Attempt to assign 'web' to a second distinct worktree app B.

scenarios.name: Return missing-upstream diagnostic and preserve corrupt route state
scenarios.setup: Stop aliased upstream cleanly and request http://web.localhost:{proxy_port}/; also corrupt routes JSON on disk and initialize store.

scenarios.name: Conservative possibly forgotten heuristic without auto-kill or unused wording
scenarios.setup: Active detached daemon running under PPID=1 with recent activity vs truly idle long-lived server with conservative staleness signals.

scenarios.name: Atomic identity revalidation, port-release verification, and two-step SIGKILL escalation
scenarios.setup: Obtain stop plan token for fixture process A, swap/simulate mismatched PID identity -> confirm stop refuses; obtain valid plan token for graceful process B -> confirm SIGTERM waits and verifies port closes; attempt stop on SIGTERM-ignoring process C -> confirm timeout notice and separate force SIGKILL step.
